posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked: I fairly routinely attempt to end a desperate Mars game by having the villain and several heroes sucked out into space. As long as one can somehow survive (Expatriette keeps an emergency air supply in her Flack Jacket, say), it can be a great way of clinching an otherwise brutal race with damage amounts heroes are often hard-pressed to match, particularly with few heroes.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Had some of the fun this evening with Final Wasteland eating villain minions.  In this case it was a Jersey Devil killing Citizens.  Which had the beneficial effect of Citizen Dawn not flipping for a few rounds.  (With better planning it might have been possible to delay it even longer I think and gotten even more Citizens permanently out of play*.)  The extra rounds allowed the heroes to gear up for a few rounds of "immune" Citizen Dawn while a pack of citizens built up. 

Once Citizen Dawn flipped back it was a short fight.  Most of a round for the heroes to take out Citizen Truth (for the 2nd time), and then the rest of the deployed Citizens were rapidly finished off, followed by Citizen Dawn herself.

Team was The Scholar, The Wraith, Omnicron-X, and Tempest.  At one point all of them had 5-6 on-going, equipment, components, etc. deployed.  Lots of synergies going - The Scholar was getting heals for Tempest and Omnicron-X and using those to plink away at Dawn or something else.  Wraith kept Citizen Dawn from clearing the board using Eyepiece.  And Omnicron-X was doing plenty with components and then keeping the Environment Deck in check as well.  And Tempest got rolling at the end with Lightning attacks.

 

* - I guess it would be possible to completely hang up the game with this villain/environment combo.  Have Final Wasteland eating citizens, but allow Citizen Dawn to flip eventually.  And then have it eat enough Citizens afterwards that the conditions for flipping Citizen Dawn back to a form that can be attacked can never be fulfilled.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
Oaktree:

Team was The Scholar, The Wraith, Omnicron-X, and Tempest.

If you named the six most powerful Sentinels characters, so the top third in terms of raw effectiveness, it's extremely likely those four would be on the list.  O-X and Scholar take a little setup, and Wraith is only "quite" potent rather than "incredibly" so, but all four are just amazing game-winning machines, held back only by low HP and/or time needed to get the ball rolling.  (For the rest of the top six, I'd say pretty definitely The Visionary, along with probably either Unity or Absolute Zero, both of which are firmly in the "if everything goes my way, I rule, but I can easily get horribly screwed" camp.  Nightmist is even more firmly in that camp and can be stupidly good, but seems to be higher-risk and higher-reward than either of the others, which I think makes her a bit too conditional for the upper third.)

There aren't any "bad" characters, save for a particular person's playstyle, but most of the rest of the heroes are more in the vein of "solid support staff" than "all-stars", except for Legacy and the Argent Adept.  Those are seldom very good by themselves, but make everyone else better.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Note - it's Omnitron, not Omnicron ;).

When we're fighting Dawn we tend to make sure there's one Citizen already out when we kill the fifth one to cause her to flip (H = 3 for us so that's all we need), so we don't have to worry about spending time getting her to flip back as she does so straight away and then we can kill as many Citizens as we like :D.

Final Wasteland would be very handy to get rid of the really annoying Citizens, though, like Truth and Chri…er, Anvil ;). But yeah, I suppose you'd have to be careful about too many Citizens getting destroyed to prevent Dawn from ever flipping back. I think that's probably something that should be reasonably avoidable, however, given how many Citizens there are in her deck and that hopefully you can plan ahead in terms of which environment creature is gonna hit which target, thereby hopefully getting only the ones you want dead, dead. And then it only matters if Unforgiving Wasteland is actually out ;).

The Chairman is another such villain where you'd need to be careful - more than three Underbosses get removed from the game before he's flipped? Whoops! Nearly made that mistake once time when I was playing Haka, and eating all the targets with Savage Mana. Fortunately I realised before I ate too many of them, so didn't need to "release" them in order to let the Chairman flip. Once he had flipped, however, I kept right on eating them :D.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Ameena:

Note - it's Omni t ron, not Omni c ron ;).

I keep getting it confused.  Might just start referring to him as #10 OX. 

Interesting with Wraith in that game is that her real good equipment retrieval card never came up until the end, and no Utility Belt either.  So round to round for her was deciding whether to hit something for 5 HP, or take a peek at the villain deck.

And The Scholar's Proverbs card with a fully loaded pile of heroes sped up the last couple of rounds.  Scholar healed, Wraith wacked Truth for 3 HP, OX healed, and Tempest did Cleansing Rains to give everyone 2 HP.  (Pity Scholar didn't have the right Elemental form going for this or he would have been making good offensive use of the additional HP flying about.)  The rest of that round was Wrath hitting Truth again, and then OX's deployed components going to town - Finish off Truth, heal three characters, a mostly blocked electrical attack.  OX's power move was blowing away the two on-going cards that were resurrecting citizens from the trash.  Tempest finished up by using Chain Lightning and a hail storm to wipe out the remaining support citizens and resume the pounding on Citizen Dawn.  Round after was mop-up.

I used to have an online buddy who went by the handle Omicron, and used a friendly robot as his avatar, so I get the names mixed up a lot too. 

But yeah, I suppose you'd have to be careful about too many Citizens getting destroyed to prevent Dawn from ever flipping back.

That makes for an amusing story all by itself…

The Chairman is another such villain where you'd need to be careful - more than three Underbosses get removed from the game before he's flipped? Whoops!

That scenario is much less resonant, but the general idea of Chairman in the Final Countdown Wasteland appeals to me greatly.  I picture him as this Mad Max-style warlord, ruling with an iron fist over a little fief of desperate survivors on the otherwise depopulated Earth.  If you picked Eternal Haka, Omnitron-X, and maybe Nightmist (on the assumption that she casts an immortality spell, or is already immortal due to the Mists) or Fanatic (on the assumption GOD SEZ SO), you could assume that the characters are the last surviving heroes, having outlasted civilization by thousands of years, and engaged in a perpetual struggle with the Chairman and his goons, not wanting to entirely destabilize the last remaining society by collapsing it into total anarchy, but impelled to try and save it from the brutality of its leader.  There's definitely a fanfic in that, if I ever find time to write it.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
So, had a couple of interesting games yesterday. First of all we got our arses kicked by about three different people. One of these was Apostate, who up till now has only beaten us once and even then we made a good go of it. This time, however, his first card play was a Profane Summons. This brought out the Effigy and the Tome, so of course then we had the Runes come out as well. The charactes in play were TLT, Unity, and Mr Fixer, in that order. We decided to risk drawing cards so that we'd have something useful (Unity had no means of getting bots out - two bots and two one-shots in her starting hand), so Tachyon chained two copies of Fleet of Foot, used her power, and had also played pushing the Limits. So Apostate got plenty of cards out there. During the three-round game spanning an epic fifteen minutes, he cycled his entire deck, with every card in play that could be in play at one point, though of course by that round's environment turn one of his Apocalypses took out all the demons and the other Apocalypse. Suffice to say, we didn't manage to destroy any of the relics. Unity didn't play a single card for the entire game, and I think Mr Fixer may only have managed one, though I can't remember for sure. We will have to have some revenge against that winged piece of excrement next time he crosses our path ;).

Two games after Apostate destroyed us, we came up against Iron Legacy. Oh joy. This was in the Realm of Discord. Angry Paul had got out, if memory serves, two copies of Superhuman Redirection, and one each of Next Evolution, Demoralising Presence, that one which gives him soak and healing and has the picture of Haka ineffectively punching him, and Galvanised. Chrono Ranger had already put Ultimate Target and By Any Means on him a couple of times and had them destroyed. Then Imbued Vitality came out and saved the day, because then we were able to destroy all his ongoings (except Galvanised, of course). Eventually, after having the bounties destroyed again, I think I managed to get out the same two bounties one last time and by this point we were a turn or two away from finishing him off, which we managed to do so even through his flipped side :). A couple of early Hypersonic Assaults from Tachyon, plus Ghostly Images putting out a six(ish)-card Lightspeed Barrage were certainly helpful, but I think the main cause of victory was all his ongoings suddenly acquiring 6hp each and becoming viable targets for Bunker's mass burning tactic :D.
